sentences.text: Ms. Priyanka Mishra - Government Advocate for the respo Heard on I.A. No.29795/2023 , first application under Section 389(1) of Cr.P.C. for suspension of sentence and grant of bail filed on behalf of the appellants No.2 (Avtar Singh) and 3 (Sonu Singh).
Appellant have been convicted for the offence punishable under Section 376 (2)(1)(F) r/w Section 5(L)/6 of IPC and sentenced to undergo RI for Life and fine of Rs.2,000/-,with default stipulations.
Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the trial Court has wrongly convicted and sentenced the appellants.
The victim has made allegations against her father and two brothers.
Father has already died while in custody.
The allegations against the brothers who are before this Court today as appellants No.2 and 3 are also same as of appellant No.1, who is no more.
Appellants are in custody since 10 years.
This appeal is of the year 2019 and there is no possibility of early hearing of the appeal in near future.
Appellants are ready to furnish adequate surety and shall abide by the directions and conditions, which may be imposed by this Court.
Hence, it is prayed that the application for suspension of sentence may be allowed.

Learned counsel for the State on the other hand has opposed the application for suspension of sentence and supported the impugned judgment 2 CRA-5656-2019 of conviction and sentence passed by the trial Court.
Heard the learned counsel for the parties.

After perusal of the facts and evidence available on record, the period of custody already undergone by the appellants and the fact that final disposal of this case will take considerable time, we are of the opinion that the application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to the appellants can be considered.
Accordingly, without commenting anything on the merits of the case, the aforesaid I.A. is allowed.

It is directed that subject to depositing the fine amount, if not already deposited, the remaining jail sentence of the appellants No.2 and 3 are hereby suspended and he be released on bail on furnishing Kartar Singh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 3 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/86935890/
1 a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) each with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court with a further direction to appear before the Registry of this Court on 16.02.2026 and on such other dates, as may be fixed by the Registry in this regard during pendency of this appeal.
